definition: Americans for Responsible Innovation (ARI) is a U.S.-based nonprofit organization focused on governance related to artificial intelligence.
details: ARI advocates for federal AI policies that protect the public while maintaining America's competitive advantage in AI research and development. The group works with lawmakers, national security experts, civil society organizations, and technology industry associations to advance bipartisan legislation.

explainer.lead: Americans for Responsible Innovation is a nonprofit that tries to shape U.S. rules for artificial intelligence. Its work matters because those rules can affect public safety, AI research, chip exports, and how the country responds to changes in jobs.

tiers.eli5: ARI is like a group speaking up while new rules for powerful technology are being written. It asks lawmakers to protect people from harms such as non-consensual deepfakes while also helping American AI research stay competitive.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers encounter ARI through policy debates rather than through software or technical standards. Its advocacy touches deepfake-takedown requirements, federal AI research, advanced-chip export controls, and workforce data collection, so teams should distinguish supported proposals from laws that have actually passed.
tiers.paperLevel: ARI is a U.S.-based, nonpartisan nonprofit organization advocating federal AI governance that combines public protections with continued U.S. competitiveness in research and development. Its documented activities include legislative advocacy, coalition building, research publication, petitions, and open letters; they do not constitute a formal technical governance framework or an evaluation of policy effectiveness.

explainer.example: In 2025, ARI opposed proposals that would have stopped states from making their own AI laws. It gathered public statements, held a press conference with state lawmakers, and led petition efforts against the proposed moratorium.

usedIn.name: Federal AI legislation
usedIn.detail: ARI backed the Future of AI Innovation Act and CREATE AI Act in 2024.

usedIn.name: Deepfake policy
usedIn.detail: It supported the TAKE IT DOWN Act on non-consensual deepfakes and intimate images.

usedIn.name: AI chip export controls
usedIn.detail: It supports controls on advanced AI chips and spoke in favor of the GAIN AI Act.

usedIn.name: Workforce policy
usedIn.detail: It publishes research and supports legislation addressing AI-related workforce disruption.

explainer.mission: ARI advocates federal AI policies that protect the public while preserving U.S. competitiveness in AI research and development. It works with lawmakers, national security experts, civil society organizations, and technology industry associations to advance bipartisan legislation.
explainer.founded: Brad Carson and Eric Gastfriend launched ARI in March 2024. They founded it to be nonpartisan and independent from the technology industry.
